gamora.bio: Sacrificed by Thanos for the Soul Stone — today's Gamora is a 2014 variant who never lived her own love story. The multiverse in miniature.

nebula.bio: Replaced piece by piece with machines by Thanos, put back together piece by piece by the Guardians. Runs Knowhere today.

drax.bio: Wanted to kill Thanos for his family and found a new one instead. Ends Vol. 3 as what he always wanted to be: a father.

mantis.bio: Quill's half-sister (Christmas reveal!) and the secret savior on Titan: her 'Sleep!' almost saved the universe.

groot.pow: Flora colossus: grows, punches, sacrifices himself, grows back
groot.bio: Died as a tree, returned as a twig, grew into a colossus. Says one sentence and means everything — at the end of Vol. 3 even audibly: 'I love you guys.'

yondu.pow: Yaka arrow — one whistle, a hundred enemies
yondu.bio: The Ravager who raised Quill instead of delivering him. 'He may have been your father, boy, but he wasn't your daddy' — one of the MCU's finest farewells.

hela.pow: Unlimited blades, killed Asgard's armies single-handedly
hela.bio: Odin's hidden firstborn, who crushed Mjölnir with one hand. Went down with Asgard — Ragnarök was her price.

valkyrie.bio: Last of the Valkyries, stranded drunk on Sakaar, today King of New Asgard. Took the throne because Thor flew off — in both senses.

gorr.pow: The Necrosword, the blade that kills gods
gorr.bio: Lost his daughter and his faith, took up the blade and hunted every god. In the end wished not for revenge but for her life — Thor raises Love today.

peggy.pow: Founded S.H.I.E.L.D.; as a variant: super soldier
peggy.bio: Steve's great love and founder of S.H.I.E.L.D. — and in the multiverse a super soldier herself: Captain Carter fought in What If and on Earth-838.

pepper.pow: CEO of Stark Industries, the Rescue armor
pepper.bio: Ran Stark's company, married Stark, flew into battle herself in Endgame — and saw him off: 'You can rest now.'

rhodey.pow: War Machine arsenal, Air Force discipline
rhodey.bio: Tony's best friend — with a Secret Invasion asterisk: part of his recent appearances was a Skrull. What was real, the MCU is still sorting out.

ultron.pow: Swarm bodies, omnipresence online, Stark's sarcasm
ultron.bio: Was meant to protect the world and decided to depopulate it. Spader's return in Vision Quest is one of the most exciting series news before Doomsday.

shangchi.pow: Perfect martial arts plus the Ten Rings
shangchi.bio: Inherited his father's Ten Rings — ancient artifacts that have been broadcasting an unexplained signal since the finale. He is in the Doomsday cast; the answer may come there.

wong.pow: Master of the mystic arts — with the official title
wong.bio: Became Sorcerer Supreme while Strange was blipped, and visibly enjoys not giving the title back. The MCU's best supporting act — in practically every project.

clea.pow: Dark Dimension magic, cuts portals into reality
clea.bio: Appeared in the Multiverse of Madness post-credit scene, recruited Strange for an incursion repair — and has never been seen since. Open thread number one of the magic corner.

mj.pow: Powers of observation, New York's driest humor
mj.bio: Knew Peter's secret, loved him — and forgot him through the spell. In Brand New Day their paths cross again without her knowing. Heartbreak with an announcement.

ned.pow: Hacker talent — and, once, sling-ring magic
ned.bio: Peter's best friend who could suddenly open portals in No Way Home and swore never to become a villain — in the comics, Ned Leeds becomes the Hobgoblin. Chekhov is laughing.

moonknight.pow: Avatar of the moon god Khonshu, multiple identities
moonknight.bio: Mercenary, gift-shop clerk and lunar avatar in one body. Marvel's best character study — waiting for a second appearance since 2022.

shehulk.pow: Hulk strength with a law degree — and control from day one
shehulk.bio: Got Bruce's blood and a better grip on what took him years to learn. Ended up literally suing Marvel's script — meta finale including K.E.V.I.N.

riri.bio: Built a better suit at 19 than some billionaires — and closed a deal with Mephisto in the Ironheart finale. The price is still outstanding.

redhulk.pow: Hulk strength, glowing red with rage
redhulk.bio: Hunted Banner for decades, became President — and exploded into the Red Hulk on live TV. Now sits exactly where he always wanted Hulk.

zemo.pow: Not a gram of superpowers — just patience and a plan
zemo.bio: Broke the Avengers without a single superpower, armed with one tape recording. His dance in Falcon & Winter Soldier got bigger than some movie openings.

ghostmcu.pow: Phasing — through walls, through punches, through everything
ghostmcu.bio: Scarred by a quantum accident, surviving for years — now a New Avenger. From the most tragic 'villain' of Phase 3 into the Doomsday ensemble.

watcher.pow: Sees every universe — swore never to intervene
watcher.bio: The narrator of the multiverse who broke his own oath when Infinity Ultron threatened to win. If Doomsday escalates: he is watching. Probably.

sylvie.bio: Stolen from her timeline by the TVA as a child, a life on the run — until she killed He Who Remains and cracked open the multiverse. Now demonstratively living a normal life with a McDonald's job.

mobius.pow: Best analyst of the TVA, unshakable friendliness
mobius.bio: The TVA agent who believed in Loki before anyone else did. In the end got what he deserved: a jet ski. Almost.

echo.pow: Photographic movement memory, Choctaw ancestral power
echo.bio: Fisk's foster daughter, who gave him a bullet and found her roots in Oklahoma. Marvel's first deaf lead.

rogue.pow: Absorbs powers and memories through touch
rogue.bio: The girl whose touch means coma — the emotional entry point of the first X-Men film and Logan's first protégé.

colossus.pow: Organic steel from head to toe
colossus.bio: The politest full-body steel colossus in cinema and Deadpool's reluctant moral coach: 'Four or five moments — that's all it takes to be a hero.'

cable.pow: Techno-organic arm, time-travel device, bad mood
cable.bio: Came from the future to kill a child and stayed to save it. Brolin played Thanos AND Cable in the same year — a Marvel double shift.

quicksilver.pow: Super speed — the kitchen scene is legend
quicksilver.bio: His slow-motion rescues are the best scenes of two X-Men films. His WandaVision appearance was the meanest fake-out of the series: not Pietro, but 'Ralph Bohner'.

x23.pow: Wolverine's clone: claws, healing factor, twice the rage
x23.bio: Logan's 'daughter', for whom he died — and who met the wrong right Logan in Deadpool & Wolverine. The future of the Wolverine line, whichever universe wins.

juggernaut.pow: Once he's moving, nothing stops him
juggernaut.bio: Xavier's stepbrother (in the comics) and the reason Deadpool got literally torn apart in DP2. 'I'm the Juggernaut, bitch' remains immortal.

tobey.pow: Organic webbing — the only movie Spidey without shooters
tobey.bio: The first great movie Spider-Man. Returned in No Way Home with back pain and elder wisdom, and kept Holland's Peter from revenge.

andrew.pow: The most acrobatic of all movie Spideys
andrew.bio: Lost Gwen and himself — until he caught MJ in No Way Home and with her his own peace. The fan campaign for a third Amazing film lives to this day.

docock.pow: Four AI tentacles with a will of their own
docock.bio: The most tragic villain of the Raimi era — and the reason 'Hello, Peter' made theaters shake in No Way Home. Was healed, not defeated, in the end.

electro.bio: From overlooked engineer to lightning god. Cooler, yellower and arc-reactor-powered in No Way Home — with the best meta line: he thought Peter would be Black.

carnage.pow: A symbiote without any restraint — Venom's red nightmare
carnage.bio: Serial killer plus symbiote blood: Venom's 'son' and worst enemy. Lasted exactly one film — hunger won.

peterb.pow: 20 years of Spidey experience, sweatpants era overcome
peterb.bio: The Peter for whom everything went wrong — until a teenager from Brooklyn reminded him why he wears the mask. Now father of Mayday.

spiderman2099.pow: Claws, fangs — the Spider-Man without spider-sense and without humor
spiderman2099.bio: Founder of the Spider Society and enforcer of 'canon events': better to allow one loss than risk a universe. Miles disagrees — part three will decide.

mysterio.bio: Sold the world a fake multiverse before the real one arrived — and unmasked Peter with his dying breath. Whether he is really dead? With Mysterio, only what you see counts.

vulture.pow: Exo wings built from alien scrap
vulture.bio: The working-class villain who turned Peter's homecoming date into horror — best car scene in the MCU. Slid unexplained into the Morbius universe via post-credits: Marvel's strangest crossover to date.

ghostrider.bio: The Comic-Con bomb of 2026: Ryan Gosling rides in as Ghost Rider in Doomsday. Which rider he is (Blaze? Ketch? Someone new?) Marvel keeps secret.

odin.bio: King, warlord, questionable father: banished Thor, lied to Loki, hid Hela. Dissolved into stardust in Norway — accidentally firing the starting gun for Ragnarök.

jane.pow: Astrophysicist; as Mighty Thor: everything Mjölnir grants
jane.bio: Discovered the Bifröst scientifically, carried the Aether in her blood and finally swung Mjölnir against Gorr — knowing every transformation undid her cancer therapy. Died a hero, arrived in Valhalla.

korg.bio: Failed revolutionary of Sakaar (only his mother and her boyfriend showed up), Thor's most loyal companion and narrator of Love and Thunder. Played and voiced by the director himself.

okoye.pow: Wakanda's best spear fighter, unbending loyalty
okoye.bio: Served two kings and a queen, stood against Killmonger and lost her rank after Talokan's attack — only to fight on as Midnight Angel. Wakanda's backbone.

killmonger.pow: Black-ops training, the heart-shaped herb, a lifetime of rage
killmonger.bio: The cousin Wakanda abandoned — who came back to take it. His 'Bury me in the ocean' remains one of cinema's great villain exits. Later appeared to Shuri on the Ancestral Plane.

wenwu.pow: The Ten Rings — a thousand years of youth and power
wenwu.bio: A thousand years a conqueror, then husband and father — then a grieving widower lured into a trap by a voice from beyond. Passed the rings to his son in death. Tony Leung's MCU debut is widely called the best villain performance of Phase 4.

highevo.bio: Created Rocket in a cage lab and a substitute Earth of animal people — and destroyed both when they weren't perfect. No cosmic plan, just cruelty: perhaps the most hated MCU villain. Alive. In a cell on Knowhere.

dormammu.bio: 'Dormammu, I've come to bargain' — Strange didn't defeat him, he annoyed him into surrender: a time loop of endless dying. The deal holds. For now. Clea's lineage leads straight to him.

ego.pow: A Celestial: a planet with a face and expansion plans
ego.bio: Quill's father, literally a planet, who wanted to coat the galaxy in himself — and casually confessed to planting the tumor in Quill's mother. That sentence cost him everything.

stane.bio: Howard's partner, Tony's mentor, the man behind his abduction — the very first MCU villain and still the template: betrayal from inside the house.

ronan.pow: Kree fanatic with the Universal Weapon
ronan.bio: Kree fundamentalist who wanted to erase Xandar with the Power Stone — and got distracted by a dance-off. In 1995 (Captain Marvel) he was still Carol's disciplined enemy-superior.

leader.bio: 17 years between setup and payoff: in 2008 Banner's blood dripped into his wound, in 2025 he pulled the strings behind Ross's fall. Warned from his cell: 'The others are coming.' He meant other worlds.

apocalypse.pow: The world's oldest mutant, collects powers like stamps
apocalypse.bio: Millennia old, four horsemen, big speeches — and in the end dismantled by Jean Grey's Phoenix fire. Oscar Isaac's second of three Marvel roles alongside Moon Knight and Spider-Man 2099: he secretly has his own multiverse.

silversurfer.pow: The Power Cosmic, herald of Galactus
silversurfer.bio: Sold her freedom to Galactus to save her world — and has been announcing the end to other worlds since. The 2007 Fox version was Norrin Radd; the MCU chose Shalla-Bal, the comics' beloved, as herald.

may.bio: The youngest, most active May in cinema — a social worker who taught Peter to help where you can. Died by Goblin's hand, but not before THE line: 'With great power comes great responsibility.' In the MCU, May says it — not Ben.

happy.bio: Tony's driver, friend and estate manager — and Peter's reluctant substitute grown-up. Played by the man who started the MCU as director of Iron Man.

sersi.bio: Loved humanity enough to stop the birth of a Celestial — and was dragged into space by Arishem for it: the verdict on Earth has been pending since 2021. One of the MCU's biggest unresolved threads.

blade.pow: Half-vampire: all the strengths, none of the weaknesses
blade.bio: Announced with fanfare in 2019, heard as a voice in the Eternals credits in 2021 ('Sure you're ready for that, Mr. Whitman?') — since then: script restarts, director changes, silence. Marvel's most famous ghost project.
